history.summary: 1BR at The Tennery, an integrated mixed-use 99LH project directly above Hillion Mall and the Bukit Panjang MRT/LRT interchange. Sound transport-connected entry at $800k/$1,303 psf, but D23 OCR appreciation is pedestrian (3.4%/yr CAGR over 128 txns) and the unit is leasehold and 13 years old.
history.rating_rationale: Strong liquidity anchors (230m to DT1 Bukit Panjang, integrated with Hillion Mall, 128 URA txns) and PSF $1,303 sits below the $1,369 district median — fair value. But 3.4%/yr appreciation is OCR-baseline-tier, the 99LH started 2010 so lease decay is now active, and 1BR in suburban D23 has a shallow owner-occupier buyer pool. Decent yield play, not a capital-growth pick.
red_flags: 99-year leasehold, ~13 years gone — lease decay drag on a long hold
D23 1BR appreciation only 3.4%/yr, OCR-typical with no standout catalyst
Niche suburban 1BR — investor/rental-dependent demand, thinner resale pool
catalysts: Integrated with Hillion Mall + Bukit Panjang MRT/LRT interchange — best-in-class connectivity for D23
PSF below district median leaves modest room

history.summary: Bukit Panjang 1BR asking $1,302 psf looks cheap but is cheap for documented structural reasons - a closed LRT station, loss to the DTL-connected Hillion Residences, and a long record of unprofitable resales.
history.rating_rationale: The dossier's -13.8% age-adj-cheap reads as a bargain, but deep data (psf_cohort_txns=32, appreciation_txns=128) confirms the discount is the market's settled verdict, not a mispricing. Stacked Homes documents 33 unprofitable transactions (avg loss -$72.7k) and identifies the cause: the Ten Mile Junction LRT at the doorstep was permanently shut in 2019 (Singapore's first station closure ever), and the project was structurally out-competed by Hillion Residences, which sits on the Downtown Line MRT with a larger mall. Asking $1,302 is at the floor of the band ($1,303-1,485) and below the 12-month avg ($1,355) - confirming softness. It is an OCR asset (favorable region per v3.4), but the region tailwind cannot offset a documented locational defect and weak demand. A 614sf leasehold 1BR here is a value trap.
red_flags: Ten Mile Junction LRT (at the development) permanently closed in 2019 - transit access materially worse than at launch
Structurally out-competed by Hillion Residences (Downtown Line MRT + larger mall)
33 documented unprofitable resales (avg loss -$72.7k) - poor capital-appreciation track record
Investor-skewed project with weak holding power; asking at the bottom of the band and below 12-month avg
99-yr leasehold (2013) 614sf small unit - limited owner-occupier appeal
catalysts: OCR location (D23) carries the most favorable realized forward base rate per backtest
Mature Bukit Panjang amenities (supermarket/dining below, MRT + bus interchange across the road) support rental floor
Post-rectification works reportedly improved the development's condition

history.summary: Re-eval under v3.4.1+ priors of a DIFFERENT, pricier unit ($900k / $1,466 psf, 614 sqft 1BR) than the 06-09 Avoid ($1,303 psf). The prior Avoid leaned partly on trailing losses (33 unprofitable resales) — a ~0-forward-power signal now discounted — and on an LRT-closure narrative that cuts little here (230m from the Bukit Panjang DTL terminus is genuinely strong connectivity). But the verdict still resolves Avoid for the opposite, validated reason: the strongest forward signal is cheap-vs-district-peers in OCR, and this ask is RICH, not cheap — $1,466 psf sits above the entire 12-month 1BR print range ($1,304–$1,418, avg ~$1,355; latest 614 sqft sale $870k Jan 2026) while multiple identical 614 sqft units in the same building list at $830k–$880k. Gross yield at asking ~4.0% ($3,000/mo recent deals) is OCR-typical, no edge.
history.rating_rationale: Ask $1,466 psf is above the top of The Tennery own 12-month 1BR transaction range ($1,304–$1,418) and ~8% above the 12-month average — the validated cheap-vs-peers OCR signal points against this unit, not for it. Identical-format 614 sqft units in the same project are listed $70–100k cheaper, so even a motivated buyer of the project should not buy THIS unit at THIS price. Confidence is high because same-project same-size comps are abundant and unambiguous; this is listing-specific overpricing, not a near-tie.
red_flags: Asking $1,466 psf exceeds the entire 12-month 1BR print range ($1,304–$1,418 psf; latest 614 sqft sale $870k Jan 2026)
Multiple identical 614 sqft 1BR listings in the same building at $830k–$880k — this is the most expensive 1BR on the market in the project
Structurally out-competed by Hillion Residences (newer, directly mall+MRT integrated, ~$1,754 psf median) for the same Bukit Panjang tenant/buyer pool
99-yr lease from ~2010 (~16 years gone) on a small investor-format 1BR — lease decay over a 5-7yr hold
catalysts: 230m to Bukit Panjang MRT (DT1 Downtown Line terminus) + bus interchange — the 2019 Ten Mile Junction LRT closure narrative materially overstates the connectivity loss for this address
OCR/D23 carries the strongest realized forward base rate (~+3.7%/yr) per backtest
~4.0% gross yield at asking (recent 1BR deals ~$3,000/mo) supports a rental floor
Would re-rate toward Neutral if price negotiated to ~$830k (~$1,350 psf, in line with prints)
history.source: re-eval under v3.4.1+ priors (2026-06-11 loop iter 9; supersedes 2026-06-09 pre-prior-fix Avoid on a cheaper unit)
